I woke up with a huge spot an my nose and I teach. Anyone like to share an equally embarrassing problem?

I used to teach evening GED courses. I had days off at the time, so I did an online Master's program, and household chores by day and taught in the evenings. My house sits on 2 acres and has a creek that splits the property down the middle. Along the creek, it's difficult to mow because it's a 5 foot drop into about a foot of water. So I usually would do the creek edges with a weed eater. I was doing that one summer a few hours before I had to teach. For some reason, along the edges of the creek are where yellow jackets like to make their burrows. I've been attacked by them on many occasions. I'm terribly allergic, and when I have discovered their dens, it has been bad for me, but even worse for them.

I had cleared them out with extreme prejudice each of the previous summers, and hadn't seen any signs of them that summer, so my guard was down. As I ran the weed eater along the creek edge, I was instantly swarmed. Yellow jackets don't fuck around. When they decide to attack you, you instantly find yourself surrounded by a cloud of them. I was experienced in their tactics at this point, so I immediately tossed the weed eater, knowing they would target that first. I ran backwards, away from the creek's edge and avoided getting stung... mostly. As I retreated, I felt a sharp pain in my right ear.

I knew what was to come. I knew I would get a fever and be sick, nauseated, and I knew there would be swelling. I also knew that antihistamines make me loopy, and prevent me from consuming alcohol. (A whole different story. Once, I drank half a beer, then took a Benadryl for a bee sting, slept for 18 hours, woke up thinking I had napped for an hour. Lots of confusion ensued. It started on a Friday evening, and I woke up Saturday afternoon wondering where my weekend had gone.)

Because I had a class to teach, and because I wanted to have some whiskey after my class, I decided to tough it out and forego medication. Fast forward a few hours. I go teach my class feeling like absolute shit and with a right ear the size of my hand. I could literally shake my head and slap myself on the side of the face with it.

Everyone in class was polite, but when class was over, one kid came up and said, "I bet that hurts like a motherfucker." It id.

I don't really get embarrassed by shit like that. Shit happens and you live on with a story to tell.

I see a few forces at work:

  1. She sounds like she's incapable of constructing or seeing a future -- which is a hallmark sign of depression. Your best bet is to suggest she go into Cognitive Behavior Therapy or maybe short-term dynamic psychotherapy. Anti-depressants aren't super helpful (decades of experience with them) and will likely push her even closer to hamness. Maybe an activating AD like Wellbutrin could work short-term. Virtually every other AD, especially mood stabilizers like Abilify, will pack on the pounds.
  2. Your wife also sounds as though she's adopted a kind of post-survival fatalism, i.e. everything is predetermined and her behavior has zero impact on what happens in her life. In her mind, she likely believes that having previously chosen healthy behaviors, including abstaining from constantly binging on dessert, did nothing to ward off cancer, so now she might as well eat whatever the fuck she wants because cancer could very well return. Essentially she's rationalizing her gluttony and interrupting that cognition is going to be damn near impossible. Be prepared for guilt, shame, crying, and denial if you try to pry that dangerous thought from her mind. "If you really loved me, how I look wouldn't matter"; "You don't understand what it's like to have to live with this," etc.
  3. Your wife, even if not conscience of the fact, likely knows on some level that with 6 years in, she's essentially fully vested with alimony, etc. That's significant and asymmetrical leverage she has over you, which could very well be reinforcing her current attitudes and behaviors. She may honestly believe "I survived cancer and I can do whatever the fuck I want and he can't do shit without dropping a neutron bomb on his life. I'll take the fucking house, all his money, his happiness, everyone will think he's a piece of shit for leaving me after cancer, etc." It may very well NOT be that bad, but you still need to consider worst case.

The best thing you can do is be honest. Anything less and you're essentially enabling her, which will just make shit that much worse. Resentment will grow and you'll hate her, which will destroy your relationship. When you're resentful and married, you're infinitely screwed because ejecting is infinitely harder with severe penalties.

You also need to take care of yourself physically and emotionally. Don't lose sight of your own identity. Hit the gym, spend time alone if you need, don't isolate yourself socially, and don't let her emotional manipulation destroy you. Remember the person you married. Hopefully she's still in there somewhere, but if she's checked out and let some dispirited vagrant move in, that's not good for you and enabling her new life of quiet desperation is terrible for her.
